segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Good morning.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: I'm very pleased to have been invited along to your club to talk about our Charity Sponsored Walking Holiday for Education Aid.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: I'll start by giving you a brief overview of what it entails.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: First of all let me explain what we mean by 'sponsored' here.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: This is where people promise to donate money to the charity if you achieve your goal, in this case to walk a certain number of miles.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Basically we are organizing a ten-day holiday, from the sixth to the sixteenth of November, with eight days actual walking, trekking in the Semira Mountains.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Let's have a look at some of the details.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: We require you to raise sponsorship money of at least $3,200, paying $250 of it up front as a deposit and the rest in stages throughout the year.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Out of this about thirty-five per cent will go on your expenses, and that leaves sixty-five per cent guaranteed to go to the charity.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Which brings me to the most important part.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: This trek is being specifically organized to help education in the Semira region.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Last year we helped train teachers for the disabled, and this year we're focusing on the pupils.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Each of the walkers' sponsorship money will go to help an individual special needs pupil in one of the mountain schools.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: In the second part of the talk I'll be giving you a lot more details, but back to the basic information.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Age limits.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: This is the second time we have run this kind of holiday and urn, on the first we even had an eighty-year old, but we found it was wise to establish limits this time.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: You have to be at least eighteen and the top limit is now seventy, though you need to obtain a health certificate from your doctor if you are over sixty years old.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Now, the Sernira Mountains are among the highest in the world but you mustn't be too daunted, we will mainly be trekking in the foothills only, although there will be spectacular views even in the foothills.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: However, you will need to be extremely fit if you aren't now and you're interested in coming with us.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: You have plenty of time to get into shape.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: You will be sleeping in tents so you must have quite a bit of equipment with you but you will be helped by local assistants.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Your bedding and so forth will be carried by them.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: We ask that you omy walk with a small rucksack with needs for the day.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: I don't think I've really said enough about the marvellous area you'll be walking in.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Let's have a look at some of the sights you'll be seeing.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Apart from these spectacular snow-covered peaks and valleys, there are marvellous historic villages.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: The area has been famous for centuries for making beautiful carpets, although recently there has been a trend to move into weaving blankets and wood carving.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: The people are extremely friendly and welcoming.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: We deliberately keep the parties small in size to minimize disruption to people and landscape.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: I hope that there are still some people interested.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: I will be distributing leaflets at the end where you can find out more information, but just for the moment I'll outline the itinerary, the main high points of the holiday.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Obviously, you'll start by flying out to Kishba, the capital city, on Day One.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: After a couple of days to acclimatize yourself, you'll start the trek . on Day Three walking through the enormous Katiba Forest which will take the whole of the day.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Day Four takes us higher up, going through the foothills past a number of villages and visiting a school for the disabled in Sohan.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Then you have a rest day, that's Day Five, before going to the spectacular Kurni Temple with twelfth-century carvings, set in a small forest by a lake and that's Day Six, the highlight for many.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: We stay near there for Day Seven because then comes the hardest day, walking through very mountainous country, but culminating in a swim in the Parteh Falls.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: This is the highest waterfall in the region.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Day Nine is much easier, with part of the day spent in a village where they make some of the gorgeous red blankets.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Then back down to Kishba and the journey home.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: So you can see it's a pretty packed timetable ...
